posts.title: California First-Time Buyer's Compliance Roadmap (REAL ID, Residency & DROS)
posts.caption_full:
California has some of the most specific statutory documentation rules in the nation — and simple paperwork oversights are the #1 reason lawful first-time applicants get turned away at the counter.

Swipe through SikhRPA's 5-Step California Compliance Roadmap to prepare every document properly:
1. Primary ID (CA PC § 26845): Check the top-right corner of your CA Driver's License! If it says 'FEDERAL LIMITS APPLY' instead of displaying the REAL ID Golden Bear & Star, you MUST bring an unexpired U.S. Passport, certified U.S. Birth Certificate, or valid Green Card (Form I-551).
2. Handgun Proof of Residency (11 CCR § 4045.1): Current DMV registration, municipal utility bill (≤90 days), signed residential lease, or property deed matching your ID address. Cell phone bills, bank statements, and internet/cable bills are strictly rejected.
3. Firearm Safety Certificate (CA PC § 31615): 30-question exam (75% passing, $25 fee, valid 5 years).
4. Exact 10-Day (240-Hour) DROS Wait (CA PC § 26815 & § 28220): Counted to the exact second, with a hard 30-day pickup expiration window.
5. Delivery & Legal Transport (CA PC § 26850 & § 25610): Complete the Safe Handling Demonstration, verify a DOJ-approved lock/safe affidavit, and transport unloaded inside a locked container or trunk.

Use the interactive counter-readiness self-audit checklist free at sikhrpa.org/buyer-guide.html (Link in bio).

posts.title: Interactive Pistol Shot Diagnostic — Fixing Low-Left (7–8 O'Clock)
posts.caption_full:
Are your pistol shots consistently landing low and to the left (7:00–8:00 o'clock)? Nearly 85% of right-handed shooters experience this exact pattern — and it is almost never your sights.

What's really happening biomechanically:
1. Sympathetic Grip Squeeze: As your index finger presses the trigger, your bottom three fingers (middle, ring, pinky) clench involuntarily, pulling the muzzle downward and inward.
2. Recoil Anticipation: Pre-emptively pushing the wrist down right before the shot breaks.
3. Trigger Finger Placement: Hooking too deep into the 1st joint crease drags the frame left; use the center pad sweet spot and hinge straight rearward.

The Fix — The 70/30 Grip Rule:
Apply ~70% clamping pressure with your support hand and keep your dominant hand relaxed (~30%) so your trigger finger moves independently.

Dry-Fire Safety Checklist (BEFORE every drill):
✓ Visually & physically verify chamber & magwell are 100% clear
✓ Remove ALL live ammunition from the room
✓ Point strictly at a safe, solid backstop

posts.title: How to Zero Optics — Centroid Triangulation, MOA vs MIL, Click Scaling & Height-Over-Bore
posts.caption_full:
Stop burning ammunition chasing single bullet holes on paper! Zeroing a pistol red dot or rifle scope is pure geometry once you understand four simple principles.

Swipe through SikhRPA's visual technical guide to zeroing optics accurately:
• 5-Shot Group Centroid Triangulation: Never adjust for one shot — fire a rested 3–5 shot group, find the Mean Point of Impact (MPI), and dial once.
• MOA vs. MIL (MRAD): 1 MOA ≈ 1.047" at 100 yds (1/4, 1/2, or 1 MOA clicks) vs. 1 MIL = 3.60" at 100 yds (0.1 MIL = 0.36" per click). Golden Rule: turret arrows ('UP' / 'R') move your bullet impact (POI)!
• 25 / 50 / 100-Yard Click Scaling: Closer targets mean smaller inch-per-click shifts — so 25 yards requires 4× as many clicks per inch as 100 yards.
• Height-Over-Bore Mechanical Offset: Because an optic sits ~2.6" above a carbine bore (~0.8" on pistols), close 3–7 yard shots naturally hit 1.5"–2.5" below your dot.
• 5-Step Field Zeroing Protocol in English & Gurmukhi (ਸਹੀ ਜ਼ੀਰੋਇੰਗ ਲਈ ੫ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਕਦਮ)

posts.title: Shaheedi Week Reflection — Miri-Piri, Sant-Sipahi & Sikh Martial Heritage
posts.caption_full:
During Shaheedi Week (Poh / late December), we bow our heads in solemn remembrance of the Chaar Sahibzaade — Baba Ajit Singh Ji, Baba Jujhar Singh Ji, Baba Zorawar Singh Ji, and Baba Fateh Singh Ji — alongside Mata Gujri Ji and the devoted Sikhs of Chamkaur Sahib and Sirhind.

Their sacrifice illuminates the deepest truth of Sikh martial heritage: strength is never rooted in aggression, vanity, or dominance. It is bound to spiritual humility (Piri), moral restraint (Miri), and unwavering protection of human dignity.

In the Zafarnama (Verse 22), Guru Gobind Singh Ji articulated the ethic that guides our educational mission to this day:
ਚੁ ਕਾਰ ਅਜ਼ ਹਮਹ ਹੀਲਤੇ ਦਰ ਗੁਜ਼ਸ਼ਤ ॥
ਹਲਾਲ ਅਸਤ ਬੁਰਦਨ ਬ ਸ਼ਮਸ਼ੀਰ ਦਸਤ ॥੨੨॥
"When all other peaceful avenues have been exhausted and every remedy has failed, only then is it righteous to take up the sword."

Today, honoring that sacred covenant of Shastar reverence means exercising total discipline: de-escalation first, strict obedience to the law, safe home storage to protect every child, and humble service (Seva) to our Sangat and neighbors.

50/200-Yard vs. 100-Yard Rifle Zero: Which Should You Choose?

ਕਾਰਬਾਈਨ ਜ਼ੀਰੋਇੰਗ ਤੁਲਨਾ — 50/200 ਗਜ਼ ਬਨਾਮ 100 ਗਜ਼ ਜ਼ੀਰੋ ਦਾ ਫ਼ਰਕ

Understanding where your bullet crosses your optical line of sight eliminates guesswork from close quarters out to 200+ yards.

• 50/200-Yard Practical Zero: Crosses line of sight at 50 yd, rises <2" at ~120 yd, and crosses zero again at 200 yd.
• 100-Yard Precision Zero: Preferred for magnified scopes — trajectory kisses crosshair at 100 yd and drops smoothly after.
• Account for 2.6" Height-Over-Bore: On either zero, close 3–7 yard shots still hit ~1.5"–2.5" below the dot.

• 3. Ventilate & Protect Eyes: Wear safety glasses against spring tension & solvents; work in a well-ventilated area.
• 4. Function Check Safely: Point in a confirmed safe direction during reassembly function checks, then lock immediately.

The Golden Rule of Optic Turrets: Arrows Always Move Bullet Impact (POI)

ਓਪਟਿਕ ਡਾਇਲ ਦਾ ਸੁਨਹਿਰੀ ਨਿਯਮ — UP ਅਤੇ R ਤੀਰ ਗੋਲੀ ਦੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ (POI) ਨੂੰ ਹਿਲਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ

Forget twisting dials backwards at the bench. Remember one rule: if your 5-shot group center hits LOW and LEFT, dial UP and RIGHT!

• Always Shoot a 3–5 Shot Group: Never turn turrets after a single shot — measure the group centroid (MPI).
• Hitting LOW? Dial UP: Turn top elevation turret in the direction marked 'UP' to raise impacts.
• Hitting LEFT? Dial R (RIGHT): Turn side windage turret toward 'R' to shift impacts right toward center.
• Zero Math Required: Plot your target hits free at sikhrpa.org/zero-optics.html.
